statement:
You are given an array `tasks` of CPU tasks, each labelled with an uppercase letter from `A` to `Z`, and a non-negative integer `n`. Each time unit the CPU either finishes one task or stays idle, and tasks may be done in any order.

There is a **cooling period**: two tasks with the same label must be separated by at least `n` time units.

Return the **minimum number of time units** needed to complete all tasks.

examples.explanation: One schedule is `A → B → idle → A → B → idle → A → B`.
`A → B → C → D → A → B` needs no idle time.
`A → B → idle → idle → A → B → idle → idle → A → B`.

constraints: tasks[i] is an uppercase English letter
hints: The most frequent task dictates the shape of the schedule: its copies must be spaced `n` units apart, creating gaps that other tasks can fill.
Count frequencies. Let `maxFreq` be the highest count and `maxCount` the number of letters that reach it. (A max-heap simulation also works but is slower to write.)
The frame built around the most frequent tasks takes `(maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + maxCount` units. If there are more tasks than that, no idles are needed, so return `max(tasks.length, frame)`.

solutions.name: Day-by-Day Simulation
solutions.description: Advance the calendar one day at a time; before each task, keep taking break days until its type was last done more than space days ago.

code.bash:
taskSchedulerII() {
    local -a tasks
    read -ra tasks <<< "$1"
    local space=$2 day=0 t
    local -A last
    for t in "${tasks[@]}"; do
        (( day++ ))
        # Take break days one at a time until the cooldown has passed
        while [[ -n ${last[$t]} ]] && (( day - last[$t] <= space )); do (( day++ )); done
        last[$t]=$day
    done
    echo "$day"
}

keyPoints: Take one break day at a time

solutions.name: Last-Day Hash Map (Optimal)
solutions.description: Since the order is fixed, do each task as early as allowed: the day after the previous task, or space + 1 days after this type was last done — whichever is later.

code.bash:
taskSchedulerII() {
    local -a tasks
    read -ra tasks <<< "$1"
    local space=$2 day=0 t ready
    local -A last
    for t in "${tasks[@]}"; do
        # Jump straight to the first allowed day for this task type
        ready=$(( ${last[$t]:-$(( -space - 1 ))} + space + 1 ))
        day=$(( day + 1 > ready ? day + 1 : ready ))
        last[$t]=$day
    done
    echo "$day"
}

keyPoints: Jump over break days at once

solutions.name: Greedy Placement Simulation
solutions.description: Fill positions left to right; at each one pick, among letters not used in the last k − 1 positions, the one with the most copies left. If no letter is eligible, the arrangement is impossible.

code.bash:
canRearrangeKApart() {
    local s=$1 k=$2 alpha=abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz i c best
    local -a count last
    local -A idx
    if (( k <= 1 )); then echo true; return; fi
    for (( c = 0; c < 26; c++ )); do idx[${alpha:c:1}]=$c; count[c]=0; last[c]=$(( -k )); done
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do (( count[idx[${s:i:1}]]++ )); done
    # Fill each slot with the most plentiful letter whose cooldown has expired
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do
        best=-1
        for (( c = 0; c < 26; c++ )); do
            if (( count[c] && i - last[c] >= k && (best < 0 || count[c] > count[best]) )); then best=$c; fi
        done
        (( best < 0 )) && { echo false; return; }
        (( count[best]-- ))
        last[best]=$i
    done
    echo true
}

keyPoints: Letter usable when i − last ≥ k

solutions.name: Max-Frequency Frame Formula (Optimal)
solutions.description: The most frequent letter (frequency f) forces f − 1 full blocks of length k plus a final block holding every letter that also has frequency f. The string fits exactly when (f − 1)·k + c ≤ n.

code.bash:
canRearrangeKApart() {
    local s=$1 k=$2 i v f=0 c=0
    local -A freq
    if (( k <= 1 )); then echo true; return; fi
    for (( i = 0; i < ${#s}; i++ )); do (( freq[${s:i:1}]++ )); done
    for v in "${freq[@]}"; do (( v > f )) && f=$v; done
    for v in "${freq[@]}"; do (( v == f )) && (( c++ )); done
    # f - 1 frames of width k, then the c letters tied for the max frequency
    (( (f - 1) * k + c <= ${#s} )) && echo true || echo false
}

solutions.name: Sorting by Frequency
solutions.description: Sort tasks by frequency and simulate the scheduling process, placing tasks in order of frequency with cooldown gaps.

code.bash:
leastInterval() {
    local -a tasks heap cycle
    read -ra tasks <<< "$1"
    local n=$2 t cnt time=0 k
    local -A count
    for t in "${tasks[@]}"; do (( count[$t]++ )); done
    # Binary max-heap of remaining counts
    push() {
        local k=${#heap[@]} p t
        heap[k]=$1
        while (( k > 0 )); do
            p=$(( (k - 1) / 2 ))
            (( heap[p] >= heap[k] )) && break
            t=${heap[p]}; heap[p]=${heap[k]}; heap[k]=$t; k=$p
        done
    }
    pop() {   # largest count -> _top
        local last=$(( ${#heap[@]} - 1 )) k=0 l r s t
        _top=${heap[0]}
        heap[0]=${heap[last]}; unset 'heap[last]'
        while :; do
            l=$(( 2 * k + 1 )) r=$(( 2 * k + 2 )) s=$k
            (( l < last && heap[l] > heap[s] )) && s=$l
            (( r < last && heap[r] > heap[s] )) && s=$r
            (( s == k )) && break
            t=${heap[s]}; heap[s]=${heap[k]}; heap[k]=$t; k=$s
        done
    }
    for cnt in "${count[@]}"; do push "$cnt"; done
    while (( ${#heap[@]} )); do
        # Each cycle runs up to n + 1 tasks, most frequent first
        cycle=()
        for (( k = 0; k <= n && ${#heap[@]}; k++ )); do pop; cycle+=("$_top"); done
        for cnt in "${cycle[@]}"; do (( cnt > 1 )) && push $(( cnt - 1 )); done
        # A full cycle (idles included) unless this was the last one
        if (( ${#heap[@]} )); then (( time += n + 1 )); else (( time += ${#cycle[@]} )); fi
    done
    echo "$time"
}

keyPoints: Use max-heap to always pick most frequent
Process tasks in cycles of n+1
Idle time fills unused cycle slots

solutions.name: Math Formula (Optimal)
solutions.description: The minimum time is determined by the most frequent task. Calculate idle slots and fill them with other tasks.

code.python:
def leastInterval(tasks, n):
    from collections import Counter
    count = Counter(tasks)
    max_freq = max(count.values())
    max_count = sum(1 for v in count.values() if v == max_freq)
    result = (max_freq - 1) * (n + 1) + max_count
    return max(result, len(tasks))
code.bash:
leastInterval() {
    local -a tasks
    read -ra tasks <<< "$1"
    local n=$2 t v maxFreq=0 maxCount=0 result
    local -A count
    for t in "${tasks[@]}"; do (( count[$t]++ )); done
    for v in "${count[@]}"; do (( v > maxFreq )) && maxFreq=$v; done
    for v in "${count[@]}"; do (( v == maxFreq )) && (( maxCount++ )); done
    # (maxFreq - 1) full frames of n + 1 slots, plus the tasks tied for most frequent
    result=$(( (maxFreq - 1) * (n + 1) + maxCount ))
    echo $(( result > ${#tasks[@]} ? result : ${#tasks[@]} ))
}

keyPoints: maxCount = number of tasks with max frequency
Result is at least total number of tasks
Idle slots are filled by less frequent tasks
